turns.t: I'm here for my injection review. I haven't got long, I've a meeting at eleven.
Understood, we'll be quick but thorough. Which injection do you have at the moment?
Adalimumab. Forty milligrams, every two weeks.
How long have you been on it?
Just over a year.
And how are your joints?
Much better than before. My hands are stiff when I wake up, but it passes in half an hour or so.
When did the stiffness last get really bad?
Not sure. Some time in the autumn? Maybe winter.
Any infections since the last visit, coughs, fevers or night sweats?
No. None of that.
Have you had any injection-site reactions? ~
A little redness sometimes, but it goes. ~
Any problems with the pen, or have you missed doses? ~
No, I'm quite regimented about it. ~
Good. And are you happy with how you manage the injections yourself? ~
Yes. It takes a minute. ~
That's useful. Have you had your blood tests done recently? ~
A month ago. The nurse said they were fine. ~
Great. I've seen the results. Your inflammatory markers are low. ~
That's good, isn't it? ~
It is. It suggests the drug is working well. ~
So we carry on as we are? ~
Yes, I'd continue the same dose and the same interval. ~
Good. I don't want to change a winning team. ~
I'll also remind you to tell us before any live vaccine or planned surgery. ~
I will. ~
Please keep to the schedule. If you develop a fever or a new infection, hold the next injection and call us.
Understood. ~
Otherwise we'll review you in six months. ~
Six months. Right. Thank you. ~
Have a good meeting. ~
Thanks, I'll try. ~
